definitions.def: to think that something is true without proof
a false belief or mistaken idea
to act on each other or have an effect on each other
certain to fail or end badly
to gather and combine things in proper order

grammar_choice.en_template: We can sometimes {{1:assume/assuming}} that the whole will be {{2:as/so}} good as each of its parts.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 우리는 때때로 전체가 그 부분 각각만큼 좋을 것이라고 가정할 수 있다.
explain: 원급 비교 as ~ as 구문 → 앞에 as.

grammar_choice.en_template: Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've {{1:brought/bringing}} on board {{2:is/are}} productive and efficient.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 예를 들어, 당신이 한 스타트업을 책임지고 있고, 당신이 합류시킨 모든 사람이 생산적이고 효율적이라는 것을 안다고 가정해 보라.

grammar_choice.en_template: It might seem logical {{1:to assume/assuming}} that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't {{2:necessarily/necessary}} true.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그 결과 그 스타트업도 생산적이고 효율적일 것이라고 가정하는 것이 논리적으로 보일 수 있지만, 이것이 반드시 사실인 것은 아니다.
explain: 가주어 It ~ 진주어 to V 구문 → to assume.
동사(be) true를 수식하는 부분 부정 부사 → necessarily.

grammar_choice.en_template: The fallacy of composition fails {{1:to allow/allowing}} for {{2:how/what}} the different "parts" interact with each other.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 구성의 오류는 서로 다른 "부분들"이 어떻게 서로 상호작용하는지를 고려하지 못한다.
explain: fail + to V 구문 → to allow.

grammar_choice.en_template: Equally, a unit {{1:composed/composing}} of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas {{2:may/maying}} lack a stable center.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 마찬가지로, 좋은 사람들로 구성된 부서가 여전히 실패할 운명의 프로젝트를 진행할 수 있고, 좋은 아이디어들로 구성된 프로젝트가 안정적인 중심을 결여할 수도 있다.

grammar_choice.en_template: When {{1:assembling/assembled}} a team with a common goal, always {{2:check/checks}} the overall view as well as the individuals involved.

jumble.answer: We can sometimes assume that the whole will be as good as each of its parts.
Suppose, for example, you're in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you've brought on board is productive and efficient.
It might seem logical to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too — but this isn't necessarily true.

The fallacy of composition fails to allow for how the different "parts" interact with each other — if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem.
Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center.
When assembling a team with a common goal, always check the overall view as well as the individuals involved.
